title: Tidebound update just went live — free browser turn-based crawler, 4th in the Ultimate AI-Powered Game Jam
author: tapturnbattler
selftext:
**Tap Turn Battler** is a free turn-based party crawler that runs in your browser on phone or PC. It placed 4th in the recent Ultimate AI-Powered #4 Game Jam on Itch, which ended yesterday, and the Tidebound update just went live.

https://preview.redd.it/5y9hoxh0dmuh1.jpg?width=1792&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=abce3df5909942fd59c2e43ef574cb3b50d9ed18

**Play it here:** [https://tapturnbattler.itch.io/ttb](https://tapturnbattler.itch.io/ttb)  
**Video about game here:** [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DtAZ\_C1QPzM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DtAZ_C1QPzM)

**About the game:** You take three of four heroes down 50 floors, with grid fights and a home island between runs. This update adds:

* a story with named heroes and two endings;
* a playable cold open;
* five guardian bosses, each teaching one piece of the final boss;
* fight rooms built around one tactical question each;
* optional first-person exploring between fights.

Since this is r/aigamedev, here's how it's made.

**Stack**

* Code: TypeScript and three.js, written with AI coding agents (Cursor and Codex). It started as a Unity VR game; the browser version is a port.
* 3D: characters from Tripo and Meshy, cleaned up by Blender scripts and bound to one shared Mixamo animation library.
* Sound: ElevenLabs for many custom sounds. The music and ambience are procedural, written in code.
* Writing and art: story lines drafted by AI from my canon, then edited. All art is generated with AI.

**What actually made it work**

1. Tests for things that aren't code. Every story line runs through a lore checker before each build. It fails the build on canon contradictions, spoilers that come before their floor, lines over length, and banned words. I check the checker too, by deliberately putting bad lines in and confirming it catches every one.
2. Bots playtest the balance. Three scripted parties (smart, greedy, and "hit whatever's closest") play 60 seeded runs. A tuning change only goes in if it also holds on fresh seeds it was never tuned on. Otherwise the agent just overfits to the test seeds.
3. Research before building. Bosses and camera modes started as written research with options scored on a 100-point rubric, then playable prototypes. First person scored 48 out of 100 for combat because it hides the grid, so it only shipped as an option for exploring.
4. Docs are the agents' memory. Each system has a design doc plus a running log. After a context reset, the agent reads the plan, the doc and the log before touching anything.
5. Checkpoints where I decide. I approved the story's tone on a sample before the other \~380 lines were written. The music had a listening checkpoint. Nothing goes to itch until I've played it.
6. Even the trailers are the game. Scripted "director" pages drive the real game in a headless browser, frame by frame, with scores generated in code.

**I'd really like feedback, especially on:**

* whether the first fights teach you enough without a tutorial wall;
* whether first-person exploring is worth keeping;
* general difficulty, does it feel challenging enough?

Thanks for reading. Gather your party, and descend.
